title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: DOREEN'S WINTER
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Doreen Lindahl, a paper mill timekeeper from Bemidji, Minnesota.
Every winter, she hid under three blankets, while her sister Carol called from Arizona: Just move down here.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE FLYER
segments.quote: There is no bad weather, only inappropriate clothing.
segments.author: Old saying
lines: One gray morning, Doreen saw a flyer. Snow Sculpture Contest. Teams of two.
Doreen laughed, in canvas sneakers.
The postmaster, Arne, told her his grandmother's old saying:
There is no bad weather, only inappropriate clothing.
So she bought real boots and snow pants, looked like a purple marshmallow, and signed up.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE FIRST BLOCK
segments.quote: An adventure is only an inconvenience rightly considered.
segments.author: G. K. Chesterton
lines: She planned a ten-foot walleye.
Day one, her first snow block fell apart on her head.
She remembered a line from G. K. Chesterton, the English writer:
An adventure is only an inconvenience rightly considered.
So she laughed, and wet the next block with a watering can, till it froze like brick.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE NEIGHBOR
segments.quote: What we do see depends mainly on what we look for.
segments.author: John Lubbock
lines: But she needed a partner.
Next door lived Lyle, a retired plow driver who mostly glared through his window.
Her library book had a line from John Lubbock, an English scientist:
What we do see depends mainly on what we look for.
So she stopped seeing a grump, and saw a snow expert. She knocked. He grabbed his shovel.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE THAW
segments.quote: We may brave human laws, but we cannot resist natural ones.
segments.author: Jules Verne
lines: For three weeks they built, carving scales with a cake spatula.
Then a warm spell hit. The walleye slumped like a candle.
Lyle quoted Jules Verne, the French writer:
We may brave human laws, but we cannot resist natural ones.
So they worked with the weather. They rebuilt at night, under tarps by day.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE LAST NIGHT
segments.quote: I arise in the morning torn between a desire to improve the world and a desire to enjoy the world.
segments.author: E. B. White
lines: The night before judging, Doreen kept fixing fins. One more scale.
Lyle handed her cocoa, and a line from E. B. White, the American writer:
I arise in the morning torn between a desire to improve the world and a desire to enjoy the world.
She put down the spatula, and they enjoyed their fish under the stars.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE CALL
segments.quote: Nothing can bring you peace but yourself.
segments.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
lines: They didn't win first place. The walleye won People's Choice.
Lyle told the paper she was his best partner ever. Including his plow.
That night, Carol called. Packed yet?
By the door hung a line from Ralph Waldo Emerson:
Nothing can bring you peace but yourself.
Carol, she said, I'm staying. Come up in February. I'll lend you snow pants.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Dress for it. Laugh it off. Look for the good. Work with nature. Enjoy it. Find peace at home.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Dress for the weather. Laugh at the mess. Look for the good. Work with nature. Enjoy it. Find peace where you are.
I tried snow pants once. My wife said I looked like a sofa sledding.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
